label: input token c
explanation: Token detector for the letter c as the current input. It fires on every step whose input is c, in both the original and copy phases and at any position, and on essentially nothing else (one stray activation on x out of about 198k x steps). It never fires on <DEL> or on any other letter or digit. Magnitude is highest when c is the very first input (t=0, which gives the maximum activation). Other c inputs, whether in the original phase or fed back during the copy, sit at roughly 0.7-0.9 of the max. Runs of c at the start of the sequence decay a little (1.00, 0.93, 0.83). On the dev split the predicate scores precision 1.0 and recall ~1.0, with activation correlation 0.99.

issues: Only minor noise. On test there are 3 missed activations, all at step 8 (two on x, one on 3), each about 0.15 of max and holding 0.0% of activation mass. There are no false positives. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
Small imprecision in the explanation: copy-phase and non-initial c activations go a little below the stated 0.7-0.9 range (0.67 shows up in the lowest-quartile examples). Not material.

The other claims hold. The feature is silent on <DEL> (0 of 500k) and on every other token. Activation rate is about 0.033 in both phases and roughly flat across t, L and orig_idx. Every top example has c at t=0 with value 1.00. The run decay 1.00/0.93/0.83 appears in the top examples. Test precision is 1.0, recall 0.99998, F1 0.99999, mass recall 1.0 and correlation 0.993.
